title: Expose Gemini reasoning effort and a default Gemini reasoning level in TermAl
outcome: TermAl users can choose a supported reasoning level for a Gemini session and set a default for future Gemini sessions in Preferences. Proposed precedence: explicit session selection, then a saved Gemini default when supported by the selected model/runtime, then Provider default. Existing Gemini sessions keep their explicit selections and existing settings load compatibly. The controls use the actual Gemini runtime integration and accurately represent unavailable choices.
acceptance: Gemini’s session options offer only supported reasoning levels, including Provider default when available. A selected value reaches the actual Gemini provider integration at its supported lifecycle point. Model/runtime changes and unsupported values produce an accurate disabled or fallback state.

Preferences persist a Gemini-specific default for new Gemini sessions. Explicit per-session choices take precedence; unset or unsupported defaults follow the provider. Existing settings and the existing Codex default remain compatible.
Focused behavioural checks cover persistence, new-session precedence and fallback, and the provider request or argv/config path used by the implementation.

The exact committed candidate has a clean independent review pair under TermAl’s review rules and is handed to integration with focused check results, artifact locators, and any provider-support limitations.
